Subject: Follow-up: PO vs Card - post-demo recap & next steps

Hi Sofia - thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our call: 

- Procurement constraints you mentioned: AP typically requires a vendor onboarding packet and prefers PO-based payment for anything > $10k.
- Smaller pilots / POC spend (under $5k/month) can usually be transacted on a corporate card.
- Marketplace billing could speed onboarding but procurement still needs vendor info (W9, SOC details).

Attachments: I've included a short vendor questionnaire and a draft SOW to help procurement rubric review.

Next steps (proposed):
1) I'll send the vendor questionnaire and SOW (attached) for your procurement team to review.
2) If marketplace billing is preferred, let me know and I'll pull the marketplace billing flow and any additional marketplace vendor IDs.
3) If procurement needs a PO, we can provide a formal quote and standard vendor onboarding docs - timeline typically ~2-3 weeks depending on procurement bandwidth.

Would you prefer to pursue marketplace billing to speed things up, or should we start the PO/vendor onboarding path?

Thanks - happy to hop on a short call with procurement if that helps.

Best,

Subject: Re: Follow-up: PO vs Card - post-demo recap & next steps

Hi Marissa - thanks for the clear recap and for sending the docs. A few clarifications from procurement: 

- Vendor onboarding: we need W9, SOC 2 (or equivalent), insurance certificate, and the vendor questionnaire filled out. Procurement will run vendor risk and legal review.
- Payment policy: for new vendors, anything expected to exceed $10k per invoice or $50k annually needs a PO and our standard vendor contracting. Smaller one-off POCs we prefer card, but monthly card spend must be approved by Finance if it will hit > $5k / month.
- Marketplace: we do use the AcmeCloud Marketplace for a few vendors. If Redwood can transact via marketplace, procurement prefers that because it avoids manual vendor onboarding in some cases - but we need to confirm whether marketplace billing includes full tax/invoice detail and whether SSO/account mapping is supported.

Action items from us:
- I'll coordinate with Procurement and get back with a list of required onboarding docs and whether the marketplace option is acceptable. Expect an update by end of week.

Sofia Martinez
Head of FinOps | FinOpsCo
sofiam@finopsco.com

Thanks Sofia - that's super helpful. A few clarifications from our side and proposed supporting materials: 

- We can provide the W9, SOC 2 summary and the insurance cert immediately. I'm attaching a vendor questionnaire already filled with the information we typically provide.
- Marketplace: Redwood supports billing through AcmeCloud Marketplace (and a few others). Marketplace billing usually provides full invoices; we can share a sample invoice and confirm SSO/account mapping. If procurement prefers marketplace, we'll surface the marketplace SKU and vendor ID so you can validate.
- Timelines: if you want to go PO route, we'll provide a formal quote and core SOW; typical time to fully onboard via procurement is 2-3 weeks assuming no major legal redlines. Marketplace can sometimes cut that to a few days if everything lines up.

Proposed next steps (my recommended order to accelerate):
1) I'll send W9 + SOC summary + sample marketplace invoice to procurement right after this email (attached).
2) If marketplace is acceptable, we'll send marketplace vendor/SKU info and request internal finance signoff to use the marketplace purchase path.
3) If procurement needs PO, we'll finalize a quote and SOW and loop in Legal for standard terms - I'll draft the quote and initiate that as soon as you confirm.

Would you like me to set a 30-minute sync with Procurement + Finance this week to walk through the marketplace example and answers? I can include Aditya (billing/product) to answer any technical billing/SSO questions.

Thanks -
Marissa

Attachments: vendor_questionnaire.pdf, sample_marketplace_invoice.pdf
